title: Pure-tensor description and coherence of the pro-etale inverse-image tensor comparison
statement:
Let $h:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse image $h^{-1}$ on sheaves of sets, rings and modules, with adjunction unit $\eta_h:\mathcal H\to h_*h^{-1}\mathcal H$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For an object $V$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $s\in\mathcal H(V)$ write $h^{-1}s\in(h^{-1}\mathcal H)(T'\times_TV)$ for the image of $s$ under $\eta_h$. Let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so that $h^{-1}\mathcal F,h^{-1}\mathcal G$ are sheaves of $h^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules. Use the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and for $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $t\in\mathcal G(V)$ write $s\otimes t$ also for the image in $(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G)(V)$ of the presheaf pure tensor.

1. There is a unique morphism of sheaves of $h^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules
$$\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}:h^{-1}(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G)\longrightarrow h^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O}h^{-1}\mathcal G$$
such that $\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}(h^{-1}(s\otimes t))=h^{-1}s\otimes h^{-1}t$ over $T'\times_TV$ for every object $V$ and all $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $t\in\mathcal G(V)$. It is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$.

2. Let $\phi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be $\mathcal O'$-modules, regarded also as $\mathcal O$-modules through $\phi$ (and $h^{-1}\mathcal F,h^{-1}\mathcal G$ as $h^{-1}\mathcal O$-modules through $h^{-1}\phi$). Let $\pi:\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O'}\mathcal G$ and $\pi':h^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O}h^{-1}\mathcal G\to h^{-1}\mathcal F\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O'}h^{-1}\mathcal G$ be the maps sending $s\otimes t$ to $s\otimes t$. Then $\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}\circ h^{-1}(\pi)=\pi'\circ\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}$, the left $\sigma^h$ taken over $\mathcal O'$ and the right one over $\mathcal O$.

3. Let $g:T''\to T'$ be a second morphism of schemes. There is a unique natural isomorphism $\gamma:(h\circ g)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}h^{-1}$ of functors on sheaves of sets with $\gamma\bigl((h\circ g)^{-1}s\bigr)=g^{-1}(h^{-1}s)$ over $T''\times_TV\cong T''\times_{T'}(T'\times_TV)$ for all $V$ and $s\in\mathcal H(V)$; it is the composition isomorphism of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] (5), and it carries the ring and module structures of $(h\circ g)^{-1}\mathcal O$, $(h\circ g)^{-1}\mathcal F$ to those of $g^{-1}h^{-1}\mathcal O$, $g^{-1}h^{-1}\mathcal F$. With the target tensor identified along $\gamma_{\mathcal O}$,
$$\sigma^g_{h^{-1}\mathcal F,h^{-1}\mathcal G}\circ g^{-1}\bigl(\sigma^h_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}\bigr)\circ\gamma_{\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G}=(\gamma_{\mathcal F}\otimes\gamma_{\mathcal G})\circ\sigma^{h\circ g}_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}.$$
For $h=\mathrm{id}_T$ the unit $\eta_{\mathrm{id}}$ is an isomorphism, and under it $\sigma^{\mathrm{id}}_{\mathcal F,\mathcal G}$ is the identity of $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G$.

proof.text: Put $L=h^{-1}$, $V=h_*$ on sets, $R=\mathcal O$, and $RI=S=L\mathcal O$, with $c=\mathrm{id}_{RI}$. These are small sites in the larger sheaf universe. By [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], $L\dashv V$ preserves finite limits and the inverse-image ring and module operations are precisely the images of the original operation maps through the finite-product comparisons. Thus take $I(M)=h^{-1}M$, with the canonical underlying-sheaf identifications $e_R,e_M$. These give the algebraic inverse-image presentation of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]: applying $L$ to the graph equality for any addition, multiplication or action gives the transported equality, since $L$ preserves products; zero and one use its terminal-object comparison. Define $T(M)=RI\otimes_{RI}I(M)$ by sheafified scalar extension and define $T(f)=1\otimes I(f)$. Hence both hobj and hmap in [lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction] hold by definition, with this specified functor $T$. Apply that statement to get a comparison $\mu:T(M\otimes_RN)\cong T(M)\otimes_{RI}T(N)$ with insertion $q$ and generalized normalization as in [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]. This application supplies all its data, rather than assuming an unconstructed module adjunction.

The tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] gives $a_M:T(M)\to I(M)$ by $a\otimes m\mapsto am$. Its inverse is the insertion $q_M:m\mapsto1\otimes m$ of [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]: $a_Mq_M(m)=m$, and $q_Ma_M(a\otimes m)=1\otimes am=a\otimes m$. The same universal property checks the latter equality and naturality on pure tensors. Set
$$\sigma^h_{F,G}=(a_F\otimes a_G)\mu_{F,G}a_{F\otimes_R G}^{-1}.$$
This is an isomorphism natural in both variables. To extract its section formula, take in the generalized normalization $Z=|F|\times|G|$, $x,y$ the projections and $z$ the pure-tensor map. The unit sends $(s,t)\in Z(V)$ to the pair $(h^{-1}s,h^{-1}t)$: this follows by naturality with the two projections and the product comparisons of $h^{-1}$ and $h_*$. The normalized equation evaluated at this unit section, followed by $a_Mq_M=1$, is exactly $\sigma^h(h^{-1}(s\otimes t))=h^{-1}s\otimes h^{-1}t$.

proof.text: Here is the equality criterion needed for uniqueness, for any $RI$-module sheaf $K$. If $\alpha,\beta:h^{-1}(F\otimes_R G)\to K$ are $RI$-linear and agree on all $h^{-1}(s\otimes t)$, their underlying abelian-sheaf adjoints are $h_*\alpha\circ\eta_{F\otimes_R G}$ and $h_*\beta\circ\eta_{F\otimes_R G}$ by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. They are $R$-linear for the action on $h_*K$ through $\eta_R:R\to h_*RI$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] with $S=RI,c=1$, identifying scalar extension with $h^{-1}$ by $a_M$ from step 2. The two adjoints agree on every $s\otimes t$ by the assumed formula. The injective Hom-to-bilinear-map correspondence of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] therefore makes the adjoints equal; injectivity of the inverse-image adjunction makes $\alpha=\beta$. Applying this to two maps satisfying clause 1 proves uniqueness. No claim that pulled-back original pure tensors locally generate on $T'$ is needed.

proof.text: The maps $\pi,\pi'$ in clause 2 exist by the tensor universal property: the pure-tensor pairing over the larger ring is bilinear over the smaller ring [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. Regard both composites in clause 2 as $h^{-1}\mathcal O$-linear maps with the common source $h^{-1}(F\otimes_{\mathcal O}G)$. On $h^{-1}(s\otimes t)$, naturality of $\eta_h$ for $\pi$ and the formula of step 2 give $h^{-1}s\otimes h^{-1}t$ in the tensor over $h^{-1}\mathcal O'$ for each composite. The equality criterion in step 3 gives the required equation.

proof.text:
For composition apply [lem-trf-site-inverse-image-composition-generators] with $\mathcal C=T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $\mathcal D=T'_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $\mathcal E=T''_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $v=u_h$, $u=u_g$. The smallness and sheaf-preserving precomposition hypotheses hold by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Identify $u_gu_h(V)$ with $u_{h\circ g}(V)$ by the canonical fibre-product associator. The cited lemma gives $\kappa:g^{-1}h^{-1}\cong(h\circ g)^{-1}$ and
$$h_*g_*\kappa\circ h_*\eta_g\circ\eta_h=\eta_{h\circ g}.$$
Put $\gamma=\kappa^{-1}$. Evaluating this equation on $s\in H(V)$ gives exactly $\gamma((h\circ g)^{-1}s)=g^{-1}(h^{-1}s)$. It is the adjunction-compatible comparison in [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] (5). If another natural isomorphism has this formula, then for each $H$ its postcomposition with $\eta_{h\circ g,H}$ has the same components on every section of every $V$; injectivity of the set-sheaf adjunction for $h\circ g$ identifies it with $\gamma_H$. This proves the asserted uniqueness, not merely existence of some comparison.

Write $L_0=(h\circ g)^{-1}$ and $L_1=g^{-1}h^{-1}$, and let $p_i:L_i(A\times B)\cong L_iA\times L_iB$ be their product comparisons. Naturality of $\gamma$ with both projections and the defining property of a product give
$$p_1\gamma_{A\times B}=(\gamma_A\times\gamma_B)p_0.$$
For every operation $m:A\times B\to C$, naturality also gives $\gamma_CL_0(m)=L_1(m)\gamma_{A\times B}$. Substituting the displayed product equation identifies the transported operation maps. Apply this to ring addition and multiplication, module addition and the scalar action. The analogous terminal-object equation treats zero and one, and additive inverses follow from addition and zero. Since the structures are defined by exactly these operation maps [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], $\gamma_{\mathcal O}$ is a ring isomorphism and $\gamma_F$ is module-linear through it. Thus the tensor transports in clause 3 are well defined by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal].

source.place: Tag 03D2 (lemma-pullback-module), operation transport through finite-product comparisons

proof.text: After the scalar identification of step 6, both sides of clause 3 are $(h\circ g)^{-1}\mathcal O$-linear maps with source $(h\circ g)^{-1}(F\otimes_{\mathcal O}G)$ and the same target. Evaluate on $(h\circ g)^{-1}(s\otimes t)$. The unit formula of step 5 changes its image under $\gamma$ into $g^{-1}h^{-1}(s\otimes t)$. The two pure-tensor formulas of step 2 change the left composite into $g^{-1}h^{-1}s\otimes g^{-1}h^{-1}t$. Applying the formula of step 2 first for $h\circ g$ and then the unit formula to the two factors gives the identical result for the right composite. Apply step 3 with the morphism $h\circ g$ and this common target. This proves the displayed composition equation.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), coherence checked using adjoints and pure-tensor normalization

proof.text: For $h=\mathrm{id}_T$, the category $\mathcal I_U$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] has the INITIAL object $(U,\mathrm{id}_U)$: its unique arrow to $(W,\phi:U\to W)$ is $\phi$. Consequently $(U,\mathrm{id}_U)$ is terminal in the actual colimit index $\mathcal I_U^{\mathrm{op}}$. The colimit is $H(U)$, with cocone map $H(W)\to H(U)$ equal to restriction along $\phi$ and with the coprojection at $(U,\mathrm{id})$ the identity. These identifications commute with restriction in $U$. Since $H$ is already a sheaf, the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies its sheafification with $H$ and identifies the sheafification unit with an isomorphism. The adjunction unit $\eta_{\mathrm{id}}$ is this coprojection followed by sheafification, hence is an isomorphism. Under it, step 2 sends $s\otimes t$ to itself, so [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] identifies $\sigma^{\mathrm{id}}$ with the identity.
